pIndexDescription: Dwarfium allows you to control the Dwarf using the Dwarf API.
pIndexFeature4: 4. Connect to Stellarium planeterium app to help select targets.

Dwarfium and the Dwarf API are in beta phase. Not all features of the mobile app are present yet.

pAboutUserDataDesc: The information entered by users is stored in the browser's database (localStorage). Since the data is stored in your browser, other users of the site will not be able to access your data. This also means if a user uses multiple browsers or devices, the data cannot be synced between different browsers or devices.

cWitmotionPolaris1: Point the DWARF towards Polaris and adjust the angle to match your altitude.
cWitmotionPolaris2: You should see Polaris in the Center of the Camera.
pFirstStepsContent: Use the DWARFLAB mobile app from DwarfLab to update the firmware, enable STA mode and take dark frames.
pSetLocationContent: Set your latitude, longitude, and time zone for accurate GOTO coordinates. Use a negative longitude west of Greenwich.
pServerStatusContent: Dwarfium is running in web server mode.
pServerStatusContent1: The proxy service must be running for telescope communication.
pServerStatusContent2: DWARF 3 video streaming also requires the MediaMTX service.
pServerStatusContent3: If you have installed the proxy software on a different machine than the server, enter the proxy IP here and check its status.

pEnableSTAContent: Connect by Bluetooth once to place your {{DwarfType}} on the same Wi-Fi network as Dwarfium.
pEnableSTAContent1: Keep the telescope powered on and near this computer, then start a Bluetooth connection.
pEnableSTAContent2: Enter the telescope Bluetooth password and your local Wi-Fi credentials. Direct connection is available when supported by the desktop app or proxy service.
pEnableSTAContent3: Choose Connect via Web to send the Wi-Fi settings over Bluetooth.
pConnectPrivateID: Use a specific device ID when multiple Dwarfium instances or automation tools share the network.
pConnectDwarfIIContent: Your {{DwarfType}} and the computer running Dwarfium or its proxy must be on the same local network.
pConnectDwarfIIContent1: After rebooting, you must first connect to the {{DwarfType}} via Bluetooth.
pConnectDwarfIIContent2: Select Connect below. Once connected, use Dwarfium for calibration, GOTO, and imaging sessions.
pConnectDwarfIIContent3: If you have used the Dwarflab app before, disable 'Set Current Device as Host' on the home page and turn off Wi-Fi on your phone to allow Dwarfium to send commands to the Dwarf.
pConnectDwarfIIContent4: Dwarfium normally detects the telescope IP address. If detection fails, enter it below.
pConnectDwarfIIContent5: Select Connect to start the telescope connection.
pConnectDwarfIIContent6: If Dwarfium reports ‘Go Live’ after a completed imaging session, open Camera and select Live.
pConnectStellariumContent: Enable Stellarium’s Remote Control plugin before connecting.
pConnectStellariumContent2_1: demonstrates setting up Stellarium's Remote Control plugin (0 to 1:40); skip the part about NINA. Click 'Enable CORS for the following origin' and enter in ' * '.
pConnectStellariumContent2_2: Alternatively, download the automatic configuration tool below. It configures port 8090.
pConnectStellariumContent3: Enter the host and port used by the Remote Control plugin, then select Connect.
cAstroSettingsInfoGainDesc: Gain is a digital camera setting that controls the amplification of the signal from the camera sensor. It should be noted that this amplifies the whole signal, including any associated background noise.
cAstroSettingsInfoExposureDesc: Time during which the sensor will be exposed to light and capturing information (energy)
cAstroSettingsInfoIRPassDesc: Allows the infrared wavelength to reach the sensor. Several astronomical objects emit in this wavelength.
cAstroSettingsInfoIRCutDesc: Blocks infrared wavelength. Useful for lunar and planetary.
cAstroSettingsInfoBin1x1Desc: Camera captures light on each individual physical pixel.
cAstroSettingsInfoBin2x2Desc: Camera combines physical pixels in groups of 2x2 (4 pixels) and considers all light captured in the group as a single pixel. Can be considered a 'virtual' pixel. This makes pixel size larger and reduces resolution by a factor equal to the binning.
cAstroSettingsInfoFormatFITSDesc: Astronomy lossless numerical file format. Can include meta data of the image (coordinates, camera, pixel size binning, filter, etc) that can be used by processing software.
cAstroSettingsInfoFormatTIFFDesc: A lossless file format, but not especifically oriented towards astronomy.
cAstroSettingsInfoAIEnhanceDesc: Activates smart algorithms to automatically enhance photo quality.
cAstroSettingsInfoQualityDesc: Quality of the image displayed on the screen for preview.
cCalibrationDwarfTitleDesc: In order to use Astro function, you must calibrate the {{DwarfType}} first.
cCalibrationDwarfWarningDesc: don't put anything on the lens at this moment.
cGotoListSelectObject: Choose an object list to begin.
cGotoListDSOList1: Large (> 15 arcminutes) and relatively bright (under 10 magnitude). 119 objects.
cGotoListDSOList2: Large (> 15 arcminutes) and unknown brightness. 84 objects.
cGotoListDSOList3: Small (< 15 arcminutes), relatively bright (under 10 magnitude), with common names. 234 objects.
cGotoListDSOList4: 118 of the brightest stars with common names, with at least one per constellation.
cGotoListDSOList5: The Solar System list includes the planets, Moon, and Sun. Planetary imaging is not the primary use case for {{DwarfType}}.
cGotoListinfo: Center shows the selected object in Stellarium. GOTO moves {{DwarfType}} to the selected object.

cGoToStellariumPickObject: You can use Stellarium to help pick objects.
cGoToStellariumList1: Import right ascension and declination from Stellarium by clicking 'Import Data'.
cGoToStellariumMoveCenter: You can gently move the Center:
cGoToStellariumMoveCenterli1: Click on buttons to move the center to
cGoToStellariumMoveCenterli2: +/- 1 min for right ascension, +/- 0.1° for declination
cGoToUserListCustomObjectsListInstructio: To add custom objects lists, create an objects list at Telescopius, download the CSV, and click "Add new list".
The lists are stored in the browser's database (localStorage). Since the data is stored in your browser, other users of the site will not be able to access your lists.
If you want to share your list with other people, you can send other people the csv from Telescopius.

cSkyLimitHelp1: Enter the sky view limit values.
cSkyLimitHelp2: The format is a comma separated list of fields, each field is the altitude angle value (can be 0) followed by one or more directions separated by a hyphen.
cSkyLimitHelp3: Objects will be included if their altitude is greater than or equal to this number for the given list of directions.
cSkyLimitHelp4: The list of possible values for the directions is: N-NE-E-SE-S-SW-W-NW.
cSkyLimitHelp5: If a direction is missing then we consider that there is no limit for it.
cSkyLimitHelp6: Here is an example of possible values: 20 N-NE, 35 S-SW
cSkyLimitHelp7: Use the Visible Tag, to see only the matching objects to your sky view
